title: Chiral Entangled-State Generation through Dissipative Quantum Dynamics
authors: Huixia Gao, Konghao Sun, Yiwen Han, Lei Xiao, Dengke Qu, Kunkun Wang, Xiang Zhan, Wei Yi, Peng Xue
abstract: Dissipation, though often detrimental to quantum entanglement, can be manipulated for the preparation of entangled states, wherein ingeniously designed quantum jump processes drive the system toward the desired steady state. Here we venture beyond this paradigm, and demonstrate a new type of entanglement generation in dissipative quantum dynamics. Combining driven-dissipative steady-state engineering and adiabatic passage, we propose a general protocol where the final entangled state depends on the chirality of the evolution path in the parameter space, a scheme that is further extendable to multipartite entanglement. By simulating the Liouvillian dynamics through the quantum Langevin equation for a pair of photons, we experimentally confirm the noise-resistant chiral preparation of various entangled states with high fidelity and concurrence. Our work establishes parametric chiral dynamics as a scalable and robust tool for controllable entanglement generation, paving the way for its applications in quantum information.
summary: The authors propose a new paradigm for generating entangled quantum states using dissipative dynamics, where the final state depends on whether the system's evolution follows a clockwise or counterclockwise path. By simulating this process with photon pairs and extending it to three qubits, they demonstrate that chiral control offers a robust, high-fidelity method for scalable entanglement generation.
main_problem: The paper demonstrates a novel method for generating entangled quantum states where the final state is determined by the chirality (direction) of the evolution path in parameter space.
main_result: Chiral dynamics provides a scalable, robust, and controllable route to high-fidelity entanglement generation in dissipative systems, confirmed across two and three qubits.
method: The protocol combines driven-dissipative steady-state engineering with adiabatic passage by simulating Liouvillian dynamics using the quantum Langevin equation for experimental realization.
model_or_system: The system uses an interacting two-qubit or three-qubit platform, where qubits are encoded in photon polarizations. The evolution is governed by a Lindblad master equation incorporating non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonians and dissipation terms.
key_observables: Fidelity ($F$) with respect to target Bell/GHZ states and Concurrence ($C$), which are monitored as functions of time and path chirality.
important_parameters: The parameters include the coupling strengths ($\gamma, \delta$), the post-selection strength $\alpha$ (ranging from 0 to 1), and the path geometry in parameter space.
main_assumptions: The scheme relies on careful design of the Hamiltonian, quantum jump processes, and the encircling path; fidelity decreases with increasing $\alpha$ due to reduced state purity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate conceptual protocols showing CW vs CCW evolution leading to different Bell states. Time evolution plots show high fidelities and concurrences maintained across varying parameters ($\alpha$) for both chiral paths.
paper_structure: The paper develops the concept by first establishing the two-qubit case, demonstrating chirality dependence via path encircling. It then extends this robust mechanism to three qubits using a hybrid Liouvillian formalism, confirming persistence across different levels of dissipation control ($\alpha$).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant for AMO/Quantum Optics as it provides an experimentally verifiable method (using photon pairs) to generate high-quality entanglement deterministically by controlling the path topology in parameter space, moving beyond simple steady-state preparation.

Figure 1(a) summarizes the central results of our work. Starting from the maximally mixed state ρ(0) = I/4, a slow closed-loop variation of the system param- eters in the (γ, δ) plane prepares different Bell states depending solely on the chirality of the loop: clockwise (CW) encircling drives the system to |Ψ+ 2 ⟩, whereas counterclockwise (CCW) encircling drives it to |Ψ− 2 ⟩. While the chiral entanglement generation is appar- ently similar to chiral state transfer close to excep- tional points (EPs), our scheme is based on more gen- eral mechanisms that do not necessarily involve EPs.
